flagship_title: Combining Smart Knife with Augmented Reality
source_file: afronding Impuls overview_dec22 BM.xlsx; Overzicht output Impuls programma.pptx
raw_row: Prof. dr. Kees (C.) Verhoef, Head of the department of Gastrointestinal Surgery and Surgical Oncology
proposal_title: Combining Smart Knife with Augmented Reality
program_description: This project has the mission to augment surgeons and their surgical instruments to facilitate and even improve cancer cure with less removal of healthy tissue and less complications. It is therefore of paramount importance to combine medical and technical knowledge in the operating room. Two specific topics are envisioned to kick start this collaborative mission. First, the navigation through the body of the surgeon is enhanced by designing instruments that incorporate preoperative imaging data directly on the operative field. This will enable the surgeon to identify and resect the tumour as a whole. The electrosurgical knife will be able to providing real-time tissue feedback and warn the surgeon during the cutting process to prevent incomplete tumour resections and by identifying critical anatomical structures like other organs, nerves, vessels or ducts

proposal_title: Deducing the cellular complexity of health and disease from liquid biopsies using advanced computational modelling
program_description: Liquid biopsies such as urine and blood carry tumour-derived material including circulating tumour cells, extracellular vesicles (exosomes) and circulating tumour DNA/RNA (ctDNA/ctRNA). This tumour-derived information can currently be captured by various types of next generation sequencing approaches, which opens opportunities to non-invasively diagnose cancer, to monitor disease progression and to personalize intervention strategies improving cure rates and/or quality of life. This project aims to leverage these opportunities and develop such prediction tools using machine learning techniques that exploit multi-omic data from the circulating tumour-derived material in clinically relevant and prospectively collected cohorts

proposal_title: Sub-cellular biopsy- A key technology to gather fundamental knowledge for effective cancer therapies
program_description: We aim to converge genetics and novel nano-engineering driven technologies to probe cellular and molecular mechanisms of the DNA damage response in reaction to cancer therapies. DNA damage inducing cancer therapies, such as radiotherapy, kill tumor cells by breaking its DNA molecules. However, cells have DNA repair mechanisms that counteract the efficacy anti-cancer therapies based on breaking DNA. Here we aim to understand these mechanisms, such that they can be manipulated to increase therapy efficacy. The Micro and Nano Engineering group at TU Delft has built instruments, unique in the world, that can enter individual cells for harvesting organelles and study them by cryoelectron microscopy and high-resolution mass spectroscopy.

proposal_title: Learning from the students: Convergence in practice
program_description: Current societal challenges often require multi-disciplinary solutions. In recognition of this observation, multi-disciplinary education programs have been set up over the last decade. However, the people teaching in those programs still have a mono-disciplinary background, and there is surprisingly little cross-talk between the students in the newer multi-disciplinary programs and related older mono-disciplinary ones. The people best equipped to address these problems are today’s students: given the opportunity, they can teach each other about their work, showing the added value of ‘speaking multiple languages’, and teach their teachers, helping them to relate to topics outside their area of expertise. We aim to provide students with a platform to do so. As a starting point, we propose to organize a small in-person conference, open to all but especially geared to the existing joint multi-disciplinary programs (Clinical Technology and Nanobiology) and related mono-disciplinary ones at all three institutions of Convergence. We envision a program with ample opportunities for students to present, meet and discuss, both with faculty and with their peers. We expect that students and faculty from different programs and institutions will discover new connections and be motivated to collaborate across disciplines both in education and research.

proposal_title: Optics and Physiology of the Eye
program_description: For students of Ophthalmology it is important to learn more physical optics. Because the eye is a fascinating imaging instrument, it is very interesting for students of optics to learn more about the optical properties and the physiology of the eye. These common interests will be met in a new joint course “Optics and Physiology of the Eye” to be offered to PhD students from the Graduate School of EMC, the Graduate School of Applied Physics of TUD and the Master Applied Physics of TUD. The course will be realized jointly by the Department of Ophthalmology of EMC and the Optics Group of TUD and is a converging educational activity that will boost the recently started research collaboration. it is the intension to start in a later phase a similar joint course in the Bachelor Applied Physics of TUD and the Bachelor Medicine of EMC. The project fits best in the theme “Technology based transitions in healthcare” because a main aim of the collaboration is to improve diffractive interocular lenses for cataract patients. The project’s primary pillar is “Education”, but it is also strongly linked to common Research and to realizing shared facilities, e.g. a set-up to mimic the eye.

flagship_title: Ex-Vivo Lung Perfusion VR-based simulator (EVLP-VR Sim)
source_file: Convergence Open Mind Summary.xlsx; Open Mind Call education projects.xlsx
raw_row: OpenMindCall lead/applicant row | Open Mind education lead row | People Database participant
proposal_title: Ex-Vivo Lung Perfusion VR-based simulator (EVLP-VR Sim)
program_description: To overcome the shortage in donor lung organs, ex-vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) technique has been successfully implemented at Erasmus MC. Per 01-01-2022 is EVLP included in standard package of lung transplantation care and the minister of VWS has ordered to educate organ perfusionists (a novel profession) on local and national level to facilitate this upcoming machine organ perfusion technique. In the next few months Erasmus MC transplant group have to generate a training plan to train these organ perfusionists. At this moment, unfortunately, a real life standardised EVLP training simulator including trouble shooting based on modern blended educational system does not exist. In this project, we would like to develop a Virtual Reality (VR) based Ex-Vivo Lung Perfusion (EVLP) simulator; EVLP-VR Sim. This simulator will include a real life simulator of the perfusion machine, the respiration machine, step by step connection, management and weaning simulation, trouble shooting of various scenario’s and a tutorial. This simulation will be based on the state of the art simulation training educational programs. This simulator integrates the expertise of clinical medicine with engineering.

source_file: Convergence Open Mind Summary.xlsx; Open Mind Call education projects.xlsx
raw_row: OpenMindCall lead/applicant row | Open Mind education lead row | People Database participant
proposal_title: From uninformed to informed consents
program_description: Paper informed consent(PIC) is an essential part of scientific research; it has the duty of informing patients, and directing them towards independent and informed decisions regarding their health. However, in the recent years and by increasing data protection regulations, this document has become very complex for the average patient. The latter is not surprising, especially that one in three Dutch citizens is health illiterate (HI) and these include low educated patients, elderly and migrants. Working with HI people often means that they are not able to understand basic health information to make appropriate health decisions, nor they are accustomed to any kind of legal form. Therefore, offering complicated forms to these people might be seen as an unethical act. Since visual media e.g. video/animation (VM) proved to be an effective tool in informing study participants rather than using PICs only, we offer a unique approach that aims to support a better information provision by generating publicly available, easily understandable VM, including assets of the PIC in different languages, as additional tool to support the process of PICs. The content of the VM will be created together with experts and fine-tuned by citizens. This approach will not only contribute to better informed participants and stimulate health literacy, but it will also show that we -as leading institutes- are aware of our duty to stimulate responsible and innovative research, and create an inclusive environment.

raw_row: OpenMindCall lead/applicant row | Open Mind education lead row | People Database participant
proposal_title: An online course for fast-track training students in MRI theory and methods
program_description: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a strong and growing field of research in the Netherlands (>350 researchers in the Benelux). It spans technical and medical domains, and students with varying backgrounds (EMC,TUD,EUR) can find opportunities for projects on MRI at Erasmus MC and TU Delft. These projects can be an important source for collaborative research lines between the convergent institutions. As there is a steep learning curve, the quantity and quality of these projects depends on the availability of educational resources that raise students’ interest and provide an effective introduction during the start of the projects. However, MRI course are not always available at the desired moments, typically have a theoretical focus, and are aimed at either technology or medicine students. We want to develop an online course that is continuously and openly available, and introduces the state-of-the-art in MRI methodology for students with both technological and medical backgrounds. The course incorporates theory, interactive visualization, code examples, and exercises. Within Convergence Health & Technology, this project falls in the pillar Education and the theme Fundamentals of Health and Disease, since it builds a shared framework of MRI theory and translates this into practical applications that support innovation.

proposal_title: Values Taking Shape: A collaborative deliberation toolkit for Convergence Squares
program_description: In Convergence collaborations, new teams with members from diverse disciplines and different institutional cultures come together to innovate. The novel technologies these collaborations create, and their application in the context of healthcare, also create new ethical situations that require deliberation to sort out. Beginning with the values that we all understand and share, this toolkit lends researchers the materials with which they can have deliberations about what they worry about and what they think is valuable about healthcare technologies; with the “Values Taking Shape” toolkits, we turn Convergence Squares into spaces for thinking about how to build a better world. With the toolkit, participants are taken through several steps in a design-based learning game, with variations for larger or smaller groups and for different contexts (workshop, team-building, to initiate value-sensitive design). Physical shapes are available for several steps, so that participants can deliberate over shared materials in a way that draw out value overlaps and potential conflicts. The “Values Taking Shape” toolkits thus present an accessible and responsible way to engage research project members, and others, in intentional deliberation about the values inherent in technology design and its applications.

proposal_title: Experiential Ethics Education: Reflecting on the Meaning and Value of Human Health Through Material
program_description: In their broadest sense, health care technologies aim to promote (physical and mental) human health and well-being. While we all have an implicit intuitive sense of what human well-being entails (and how it can be promoted through health care technologies) there are in fact heated debates about what human well-being is and how it ought to be promoted. These debates often use abstract ethical theories as their currency; our project aims instead to develop an experiential materially-focused design exercise through which students engage, in a hands-on creative way, with the nature and normativity of human health in contexts of disability, rehabilitation, and illness. Scholarly readings on human enhancement and crip technoscience will give background for tinkering with existing biomedical artefacts, encouraging students to articulate how such tinkering and redesigning of the object encourages reflection on human well-being and health. Our exercise will be embedded and assessed in three different engineering ethics courses, taught to students from TU Delft, Erasmus University, and Leiden University. It will thus be tested as a prototype for participatory approaches to educating students in ethics issues that arise with emerging medical technologies at points of convergence between approaches to research, development and application in healthcare.

source_file: Convergence Open Mind Summary.xlsx; Open Mind Call education projects.xlsx
raw_row: OpenMindCall lead/applicant row | Open Mind education lead row | People Database participant
proposal_title: Student prescribing assessment system
program_description: Junior doctors are more likely to make prescribing errors than senior doctors. Prescribing errors can lead to patient dissatisfaction, unnecessary side-effects, hospital admissions, disability and even death. One explanation for the amount of prescribing errors made by junior doctors is that students are not assessed on their prescribing skills in an authentic situation during their medical training. This is due to the lack of an educational tool. By developing a life-like web-based student prescribing system in which students can do their assessments, students will be assessed more realistically. A more authentic assessment will lead to improved learning outcomes, a more realistic and intuitive insight in prescribing and thus better equipped doctors when it comes to prescribing skills.

proposal_title: The “Data in health sciences” master class
program_description: Healthcare research has always relied on data for building and testing hypotheses as well as for drawing conclusions and writing (medical) guidelines. Data about demographics (e.g. census data and life tables) and the behaviour of people (e.g. experiments in medicine and psychology), help us to better understand (un)healthy behaviour. It was however the emergence of e-commerce and Internet search engines that sparked the recent Big Data revolution and hence the development of data science as an interdisciplinary field. Using scientific methods, processes, algorithms and systems to extract knowledge and insights from structured and unstructured data, data science has become crucial for healthcare research. Nevertheless, data science as a professional skill is only superficially covered in most health-related university courses. We therefore propose the development of in-depth educational material, teaching young scholars and early career professionals to transform a broad range of relevant data sources into understandable and actionable knowledge in healthcare. Our aim is to make use of the existing health-tech knowledge of the TU Delft, Erasmus MC, and Erasmus University Rotterdam to offer a master class about “Data & Health”, facilitating the convergence of these three institutions into an excellence centre for data-driven health sciences.

proposal_title: A convergence course on “digital transformation in healthcare”
program_description: Digitalization of healthcare entails not only the development of new digital technologies, but the digital transformation of the healthcare ecosystem and various organizations therein. New technologies are shaping physician-patient relationship, diagnosis, and treatment. These changes in the value chain, forces organizations to build digital strategies and forge an organizational culture to breed innovations. Moreover, digital transformation mandates an ecosystem where several stakeholders collaborate. Mirroring this mandate, we are working more with researchers with different backgrounds, from various organizations such as Erasmus MC, Erasmus University Rotterdam and TU Delft. To ensure productivity of these collaborations, it is important to be aware of the requirements and impacts of changes of the digital era in the healthcare system. Achieving this goal calls for a common language for all researchers. Consequently, we aim to develop a repeatable course on digital transformation in healthcare, which includes modules that can empower the researchers from the aforementioned three universities for future collaborations.

proposal_title: Problem-based Project Learning to Converge Health & Technology for medical students
program_description: It seems too good to be true. A physician as medical expert with an eye for technological advances, societal issues, and with clear vision on health policy and management. Yet, exactly this is the profile of the next-generation physicians of the ErasmusMC: ErasmusArts2030 (EA2030). The strength of EA2030 does not lie in mastering all of these core competencies. It is the reflection on his or her own knowledge and skills that makes the ErasmusArts2030 realize that it is impossible as a single physician to meet all these competences. That is why, through all years of EA2030, these physicians of the future are convergent-minded and given the opportunity to shape their academic profile in an interdisciplinary fashion through Problem-based Project Learning (PPL). By zooming in on pressing societal issues from different perspectives, the ErasmusArts2030 is future-proof and fit for a society where health and technology are converging to optimize health for patients and populations.

proposal_title: Convergence course: Causal inference from a machine learning perspective
program_description: Improving healthcare requires both an improved understanding of disease processes and an understanding which actions will lead to the best outcomes for patients. Causal reasoning plays a role in both of these and is therefore essential in many of the technologies developed within the convergence programme. Given this importance we will develop a convergence course to familiarize medical researchers and data scientists with methodologies and algorithms for causal inference from a machine learning perspective. This course will prepare participants to conduct causal analysis within their research area and/or analyse their current research problem from a causal perspective. This will bring a bigger awareness within the Convergence Health & Technology community (e.g., in all themes) of many of the facets and intricacies that come into play with any causal analysis. We will cover machine learning and causal methods and tools that are relevant for tackling several healthcare and technological challenges ranging from causal effects estimation to causal discovery algorithms. This course encourages interactive discussion that facilitates exchange of ideas and collaboration.
